title: Combining present, near future and imperfect

tips.title: Three time frames, three shapes
tips.body: *Avant, je **faisais** … · maintenant, je **fais** … · l'année prochaine, je **vais faire** …* Imperfect for how things were, present for now, near future for next. Once the marker is written, the tense is decided.

tips.title: The imperfect stem comes from nous
tips.body: *Nous faisons → je **fais**ais. Nous allons → j'**all**ais.* Cut *-ons* off the **nous** form and add *-ais, -ais, -ait, -ions, -iez, -aient*. Only **être** breaks it: *j'**ét**ais*.

tips.title: Aller does two jobs
tips.body: *Je **vais** au collège à pied* is the present of *aller*. *Je **vais aller** au lycée* is the near future of *aller*. Seeing *vais* does not tell you the tense — what follows it does.

tips.title: The three-tense sentence
tips.body: *Avant, je détestais les maths, mais maintenant je les trouve intéressantes, et l'année prochaine je vais les continuer.* One sentence, three markers, three tenses. Learn the shape and drop your own content in.

tips.title: C'était, c'est, ça va être
tips.body: The opinion moves with the tense: *c'**était** dur* (then), *c'**est** intéressant* (now), *ça **va être** difficile* (next). Adding the right one after each half doubles the time frames on show for almost no effort.

steps.title: Les trois temps côte à côte
steps.body:
This topic puts the **imperfect**, the **present** and the **near future** in the same answer. Each has a shape you already know.

**Imperfect** — how things **were**, or what you **used to** do. Stem = the *nous* form minus *-ons*, endings *-ais, -ais, -ait, -ions, -iez, -aient*. *Je faisais, on finissait, il y avait, c'était.* Only *être* is irregular: *j'étais*.

**Present** — how things **are** now: *je fais, on finit, il y a, c'est*.

**Near future** — what you **are going to** do: *aller* + infinitive. *Je vais faire, on va finir, il va y avoir, ça va être*.

**The same verb across the three**:

- *faire*: je faisais · je fais · je vais faire
- *aller*: j'allais · je vais · je vais aller
- *être*: j'étais · je suis · je vais être

Notice *aller*: *je vais* is its **present**, and *je vais aller* is its **near future**. The word *vais* alone does not fix the tense — what comes after it does.

accepted: je faisais

steps.title: Les marqueurs décident
steps.body:
Each tense has its own **markers**, and they do not overlap. Write the marker first and the verb follows.

**Imperfect**: *avant, autrefois, quand j'étais petit(e), quand j'étais à l'école primaire, à l'époque, à ce moment-là* — and habit words *tous les jours, souvent, d'habitude* when the whole passage is in the past.

**Present**: *maintenant, aujourd'hui, en ce moment, cette année, d'habitude* (in a present passage), *tous les jours* (in a present passage).

**Near future**: *l'année prochaine, le mois prochain, plus tard, après le collège, bientôt, quand je serai plus grand* — and *demain, ce soir* for the near term.

**The classic shape**: *Avant, je **détestais** les maths, mais maintenant je les **trouve** intéressantes, et l'année prochaine je **vais** les **continuer**.*

**A comparison of amounts**: *à l'école primaire, on **avait** une heure de devoirs; maintenant on **en a** trois* — from 1 hour to 3, a rise of 2.

**A caution**: *d'habitude* and *tous les jours* belong to whichever time frame the passage is in — past habit (imperfect) or present habit (present). The surrounding markers settle it.

steps.title: Les pièges à surveiller
steps.body:
**Negatives** wrap the conjugated verb, which is a different word in each tense:

- imperfect: *je **ne** faisais **pas**…*
- present: *je **ne** fais **pas**…*
- near future: *je **ne vais pas** faire…*

And after all three, *des / du / de la* → **de**: *je n'avais pas **de** devoirs*.

**Reflexives** keep the pronoun matched to the subject: *je **me** levais · je **me** lève · je vais **me** lever*.

**Object pronouns** keep their slot too: *je **les** détestais · je **les** trouve intéressantes · je vais **les** continuer*.

**Être is the only irregular imperfect stem** — *j'étais* — and it stays irregular in every sentence.

**Do not mix the perfect in by accident.** This topic asks for the **imperfect** for the past: *avant, je faisais* (habit), not *j'ai fait* (one event). If you want a single event, the perfect is correct — but say so with *un jour* or *une fois*.

**Opinions move with the tense**: *c'était dur · c'est intéressant · ça va être difficile*.

**Linking the frames**: *par contre, alors que* (whereas), *donc, alors, tandis que, en revanche*. A link between two frames turns a list into a comparison.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.body:
**Part A.**

1. Write *faire* in all three tenses with *je*.
2. Sort these markers: *avant, maintenant, l'année prochaine, quand j'étais petit, plus tard, en ce moment*.
3. Write *I was, I am, I am going to be*.

**Part B.**

4. Write the three negatives of *aimer* with *je*.
5. Write *se lever* in all three tenses with *je*.
6. Write one sentence in each tense about school.

**Part C.**

7. Write the three-tense sentence shape about one subject.
8. Add *c'était*, *c'est* and *ça va être* to three halves.
9. Write six sentences about your school life: two in the imperfect, two in the present, two in the near future, with one negative and one comparison.

For question 9, underline each verb and check it against the marker before it.

props.title: One sentence per row, in the tense the marker demands

steps.title: Going deeper
steps.body:
**Use all three deliberately.** Examiners are counting time frames. A paragraph in one tense caps in the middle band however accurate it is.

**Front the marker.** *Quand j'étais à l'école primaire, …* *L'année prochaine, …* It fixes the frame before the verb and stops you slipping mid-sentence.

**Build the imperfect from nous.** *Nous prenons → je prenais*; *nous buvons → je buvais*. Verbs that are irregular in the present are regular here, and *être* is the only exception.

**Do not let vais confuse you.** *Je vais au collège* (present) against *je vais aller au lycée* (near future). What follows *vais* decides it.

**Put the negative round the right word.** *Je ne faisais pas*, *je ne vais pas faire* — the conjugated verb, never the infinitive.

**Carry pronouns through.** *Je les détestais / je les trouve / je vais les continuer.* The pronoun keeps its slot in every tense, and doing it three times in one answer is strong evidence of control.

**Link the frames, do not just list them.** *Avant, je détestais les maths, **alors que** maintenant je les adore.* *Alors que* and *par contre* turn three sentences into one argument.

**Move the opinion.** *C'était dur, c'est intéressant, ça va être difficile.* Three opinions in three frames, at almost no cost.

**Add the perfect only on purpose.** *Un jour, j'ai changé d'école* is a single event and belongs in the perfect. Slipping into it for a habit is the error this topic is guarding against.

steps.title: Summary
steps.body:
- **Imperfect** — how things were, or used to be. Stem = *nous* form minus *-ons*; endings *-ais, -ais, -ait, -ions, -iez, -aient*. Only *être* is irregular: *j'étais*.
- **Present** — how things are now.
- **Near future** — *aller* + infinitive.
- *Je faisais · je fais · je vais faire.*
- *Je vais* = present of *aller*; *je vais aller* = near future.
- Markers: *avant, quand j'étais petit(e), autrefois, à l'époque* → imperfect; *maintenant, en ce moment, aujourd'hui* → present; *l'année prochaine, plus tard, après le collège, bientôt* → near future.
- Negatives wrap the conjugated verb: *je ne faisais pas · je ne fais pas · je ne vais pas faire*.
- *Des → de* after any negative.
- Reflexives and object pronouns keep their slot in all three.
- Opinions move: *c'était · c'est · ça va être*.
- Link with *alors que, par contre, tandis que, donc, en revanche*.
- Use the **perfect** only for a single event, flagged by *un jour* or *une fois*.

examTechnique.body:
Show the **imperfect**, the **present** and the **near future** in one answer, each announced by a fronted marker: *quand j'étais petit(e)* / *maintenant* / *l'année prochaine*.

Build the imperfect from the *nous* form (only *être* is irregular), wrap *ne … pas* round the conjugated verb in each tense, carry reflexive and object pronouns through, move the opinion with *c'était / c'est / ça va être*, and link the frames with *alors que* rather than listing them.
examinerErrors: Writing the whole answer in one tense.
A marker that does not match the tense after it.
Building the imperfect stem from the infinitive.
The perfect for a past habit.
examTechnique.grade9Looks: A grade 9 answer moves between the imperfect, present and near future several times, each change signalled by a fronted marker, and never mismatches the two. Imperfect stems come from the *nous* form with *être* as the one exception, negatives wrap the right word in each tense, and reflexive and object pronouns keep their slot throughout. The opinion moves with the frame, and *alors que* or *par contre* links then to now rather than simply listing them.
